data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The key distinction is one of abstraction level, not of logical strength: idempotency is a property of the operation's semantic interface (what it computes: f(f(x))=f(x)), while safety is a property of the operation's implementation (how it executes: no harmful side effects during any single or repeated invocation). For an append-only event log, the log as a data structure only observes the semantic interface of writers \u2014 it sees append(event) calls and their effect on log state. It cannot observe implementation-level safety. Therefore the log must require idempotency (a property it can check and enforce at its abstraction level), while safety is the writer's own internal responsibility. Requiring 'safety' at the log level is a category error: the log has no visibility into the writer's internal execution.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log's replay process invokes writer-supplied callbacks or hooks (not just appending events), then the log does observe implementation-level behavior and safety becomes relevant at the log level.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'safety' is defined at the semantic level (no observable additional effect), it coincides with idempotency and the abstraction-level distinction collapses.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log is responsible for end-to-end system correctness (not just its own replay), then it must care about the writer's safety properties, not just its own idempotency.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The log enforces its contract through its interface: it accepts append(event) calls and guarantees deterministic replay. The only property it can verify or require at this interface is that append(event) called twice produces the same log as called once \u2014 idempotency. Whether the writer's internal implementation is 'safe' (doesn't corrupt its own memory, doesn't send duplicate notifications, etc.) is invisible to the log and irrelevant to the log's replay guarantee. The log's survival under at-least-once delivery depends solely on the idempotency of the append operation as observed at the log's interface.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
